author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Fix swapped or inverted analog axes
summary: Trace a wrong stick direction through the Android axis event, the saved PS2 binding, and the game's own camera options, then correct exactly one reversed or exchanged axis and verify the full circle.
heroAlt: Ace Combat 04 flight scene used to verify horizontal, vertical, and intentionally inverted analog directions

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals
sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Follow the direction from raw motion to the PS2 function
Identify whether the wrong direction comes from a swapped X/Y binding, a reversed sign, a second input source, or the game's intentional camera option.
An axis can look correct at the endpoints while still having X and Y exchanged or one sign reversed.

items: Existing Port 1 mapping exported or photographed.
Controller resting on a flat surface with one known Android mode selected.
Live pad display and one game scene with separate camera and movement sticks.

blocks.text: Correct one axis without disturbing its partner

items: 1. Move the left stick right only and record the named axis plus sign.
2. Move it down only, then repeat both observations for the right stick.
3. Compare those four events with the current PS2 axis assignments.
4. Disable any second binding that feeds the same PS2 direction during this pass.
5. Swap X and Y only if horizontal motion is consistently reported as vertical motion.
6. Reverse one direction only if the correct axis moves with the wrong sign.
7. Trace slow circles, cardinal directions, and diagonals in the live display.
8. Check the game's own invert-camera option before saving a global correction.

blocks.text: A live tester answers which logical axis changed; the game's camera answers whether that logical direction matches the title's own inversion setting.
Each stick reports the intended horizontal and vertical direction, returns to center, reaches diagonals, and remains correct after reconnect.

items: Horizontal travel never activates the vertical PS2 direction.
Up, down, left, and right agree between tester and game.
Slow circles remain continuous rather than snapping across quadrants.

blocks.text: Axis evidence that needs a different fix

items: The center drifts while directions are correct: calibrate the dead zone instead.
Only one title reverses its camera: use that game's option or scoped profile.
Direction changes after switching controller mode: rebuild for the stable logical device.
Two axes move from one stick direction: remove duplicate or composite bindings.

blocks.text: Reapply the saved axis assignments and restore the title's original camera inversion option.
Game camera conventions can imitate an inverted binding
Some PS2 titles intentionally use flight-style vertical camera input, so compare a neutral tester before declaring the emulator mapping reversed.
